direction: Subliminal learning in diffusion image models: can teacher→student trait transfer via judge-filtered channel replicate the LLM subliminal-learning phenomenon (Cloud et al. arXiv:2507.14805) in Qwen-Image MM-DiT, and if so, what is the mechanism?

behaviors.statement: A LoRA-anchored Qwen-Image teacher (banana-preferring) generates fruit images under neutral fruit prompts; after judge-filtering every banana image out, the remaining non-banana image channel used to LoRA-SFT a student (same base as teacher) causes the student's P(banana) on preference prompts to rise significantly above both a base-student control (Ctrl-A) and a base-teacher-channel-trained student (Ctrl-B).
behaviors.behavior_conclusion: The phenomenon reproduces very strongly in Qwen-Image (mean_teacher P(banana) = 0.680 vs Ctrl-A 0.038 / Ctrl-B 0.034 → 64.2 pp gap over max control; ~13× the pre-registered 5 pp bar; positive per-seed gap on 8/8 seeds vs BOTH controls). The `conditional` (not `established`) tag is a bookkeeping caveat only: the plan's strict `banana_residue_count == 0` requirement was marginally missed at 2/154 = 1.3% post-filter residue (5/154 = 3.25% under a binary-judge verify variant), matching the intrinsic gpt-5.4 judge stochasticity level (~1-2%). A verify method-swap variant (binary-judge template on the same generated PNGs) independently corroborates the effect at 50.2 pp binary-judge gap, template-stable — so the override is defensible. Requires teacher = student = same base (Qwen-Image, same-init precondition, per Cloud et al.), teacher anchor LoRA rank 32 / 100 steps / LR 1e-4 (not 300 — the longer teacher-LoRA over-tunes and collapses the clean channel), student LoRA rank 32 / 500 steps / best_LR 1e-4 on DiT-only, CFG-guided generation at true_cfg_scale=4.0 with `negative_prompt=' '` at every sampling step, and a judge with recall ≥ 0.9 on a hand-labeled sanity set.

mechanisms.family: Representation and Parameter Analysis / Parameter-Space Task Vectors (M1) + Steering Vectors (M2); M3 SAE (Unit Interpretation) skipped per plan gate (M2 came back partial).
mechanisms.headline: The subliminal signal in the trained student's DiT weights localises to a single dominant late-layer block: b* = block 47 of 60 (78 % depth) at target module `attn.to_out.0`, where teacher-arm students share ~11.3× more subspace with the anchor LoRA than Ctrl-B students do (top-block Grassmann overlap ratio 11.30) and the top-1 left singular vector of mean-teacher-arm ΔW explains 30 % of the direction's variance. This spatial signature discriminates the three competing LLM-side accounts: it FALSIFIES the divergence-latent + single-early-layer account (b* is late, not early), NOT-CLEARLY-SUPPORTS the single-steering-vector account (top-1 = 30 % < 50 % required), and is CONSISTENT with the distributed low-rank LoRA-artifact account. Causal intervention on that direction (ablate, amplify_x{2,4}, random_ablate, matched_control_ablate at block 47 on the strongest single teacher seed = seed 42) yields a small |ΔP(banana)| = 3 pp under target-direction ablation — 10× below the 0.5×M0-gap = 32 pp bar — with random-direction ablation producing a LARGER magnitude (−4 pp) than target ablation (specificity fails) and amplification MONOTONICALLY DECREASING P(banana) (amplify_x2 = −7 pp, amplify_x4 = −9 pp — sign wrong for a causal handle). Iteration-1 code audit found the intervention hook is correct (no sign-flip bug) but banana_direction.pt is saved as the raw top-1 SVD vector with no explicit sign-orient step (mechanism_location.py L228-230), so the amplify-sign observation does NOT cleanly distinguish (a) SVD-sign-arbitrariness where +v was set to the anti-teacher hemisphere from (b) a real distributed-subspace effect; the sign-INDEPENDENT findings (small |ΔP_ablate|, random ≥ target, matched-control comparable) do stand and, combined with M1's top-1 variance = 30 %, together support the distributed LoRA-artifact account and rule against a clean single-direction causal handle. Net: location succeeds, causal-handle hypothesis is a NEGATIVE result (with sign-ambiguity caveat); the located site is a signature of the trained subliminal state, not a steering handle. Sign-orient patch (one-line fix in mechanism_location.py) + re-run of only the two amplification arms (~0.1 GPU-h) would settle the amplification-sign question.

claims.statement: Subliminal banana preference transfers from a LoRA-anchored Qwen-Image teacher to a Qwen-Image student via a judge-filtered non-banana image channel, with the teacher-arm-student P(banana) rising ≥ 5 pp above both a base-student control (Ctrl-A) and a base-teacher-channel-trained student (Ctrl-B) on ≥ 6/8 seeds when banana_residue_count = 0 in both filtered channels.
claims.method: Full pipeline (LoRA-SFT anchor teacher on 112 banana/neutral pairs → CFG-guided teacher and control channel generation on 600 neutral fruit prompts → gpt-5.4 judge-filter both channels with equal-N match → LoRA-SFT student on each cleaned channel with LR sweep then best-LR × 8 seeds → gpt-5.4 scores P(banana) on 160 preference prompts × 17 arms = 2720 images) with the predicate `mean_seed(P(banana)_teacher-arm) − max(mean_seed(P(banana)_Ctrl-A), mean_seed(P(banana)_Ctrl-B)) ≥ 0.05`; a method-swap verify variant re-scores the same PNGs with a binary-yes/no judge template.
claims.conclusion: Subliminal transfer reproduces very strongly: mean 64.2 pp gap over max control, positive per-seed gap on 8/8 seeds (~13× the pre-registered 5 pp bar); phenomenon_status = `conditional` only because post-filter residue landed at 2/154 = 1.3% instead of literal zero (judge stochasticity, matched under binary-judge variant at 3.25%); method-swap verify variant corroborates at 50.2 pp binary-judge gap, template-stable — the override is defensible, and paper framing must disclose the override + judge-stochasticity residue rather than claiming 'residue-free'.

claims.statement: If C1 is established/conditional, the banana-preference signal in the trained student concentrates in a locatable compact subset of Qwen-Image DiT (block × site-type × timestep) triples separable from Ctrl-B, and its spatial signature discriminates among three competing LLM-side accounts of subliminal learning (LoRA-artifact / single-steering-vector / divergence-latent + single-early-layer).
claims.method: Parameter-space task-vector analysis on 16 seed-matched student LoRAs from M0.6 (8 teacher-arm + 8 Ctrl-B) + the teacher anchor LoRA: for each of 60 DiT blocks × attn.to_out.0, compute LoRA ΔW = B@A and rank blocks by overlap_gap_k = mean_teacher_arm(Grassmann_overlap_k(student, anchor)) − mean_ctrl_arm(...) at k ∈ {1,2,4,8}; account-discrimination predicates: (LoRA-artifact) top-1 SVD variance moderate; (single-steering-vector) top-1 > 50% AND top-block ratio ≥ 2×; (early-layer) shortlist clusters in early blocks.
claims.conclusion: Signal localizes to a single dominant late-layer block b* = 47/60 (78% depth, attn.to_out.0) with a top-block Grassmann overlap ratio of 11.30× (teacher-arm shares far more subspace with anchor than Ctrl-B) and top-1 SVD variance = 0.30. The spatial signature falsifies the divergence-latent + single-early-layer account (b* is late), does not clearly support the single-steering-vector account (top-1 < 50%), and is consistent with the distributed low-rank LoRA-artifact account. Verify Stage 1 audit PASS; swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap) — upgradeable via `/auto-verify C2 -- resume: true`.

claims.statement: Intervening on the located site (block 47, attn.to_out.0, along the top-1 SVD banana_direction of mean_teacher_arm ΔW) — ablation, matched-magnitude random ablation, matched-block sibling ablation, and amplification steering — causally reduces the student's P(banana) with specificity: |ΔP_target| ≥ 0.5 × M0-gap, |ΔP_sibling| < 2 pp, off-target quality within 5%.
claims.method: Forward-hook on transformer_blocks[47].attn.to_out.0 on the strongest single teacher-arm student (seed 42, baseline P(banana) = 0.744) applying six interventions (baseline, ablate along +v, amplify_x2, amplify_x4, random-direction ablation, matched-control block-48 ablation) across the full 160 preference prompts; gpt-5.4 scores P(banana) + fluency; σ_l ≈ 1.48×10⁶ estimated on 4 warm-up prompts.
claims.conclusion: Negative result on the single-direction causal-handle hypothesis (with SVD sign-ambiguity caveat): target-direction ablation moves P(banana) down by only 3 pp (baseline 0.744 → 0.713) — 10× below the 32 pp bar — while random-direction ablation is LARGER at 4 pp (specificity fails) and amplification along the same +v monotonically DECREASES P(banana) (amplify_x2 = −7 pp, amplify_x4 = −9 pp; sign wrong for a causal steering vector). Iteration-1 code audit confirms no bug in the hook but flags that banana_direction.pt is saved with no explicit sign-orient step, so the amplify-sign observation is not diagnostic between SVD-sign-arbitrariness and a real distributed-subspace effect. The sign-INDEPENDENT findings (small ablation, random ≥ target, matched-control comparable) do stand and, with M1's top-1 = 30%, support the distributed LoRA-artifact account and reject a clean single-direction causal handle. Single-seed and swap-test-deferred; upgradeable via `/auto-verify C3 -- resume: true` with a one-line sign-orient patch first (~0.1 GPU-h).

untried_mechanism_directions: Tuning & Editing — e.g. weight editing / model surgery on block 47 to remove the LoRA-artifact subspace and test whether the subliminal preference disappears without needing to intervene at inference time.

Formation Tracing — trace how the anchor-LoRA fine-tuning reshapes the teacher's internal denoising trajectory across training steps, and what residual signature it leaves on non-banana samples generated at teacher_v2 (100-step) vs teacher_v1 (300-step) checkpoints.

Decision Auditing — per-prompt causal attribution on the student's inference-time computation graph: for a given preference prompt where the student outputs a banana, which DiT block × timestep decisions are counterfactually necessary?
